messages.content: In a texas holdem game, Who won in the poker game with players Alex, Sam, Robert and Steve given the cards Alex':['A of spades', 'K of spades'], 'Sam': ['2 of diamonds', '3 of clubs'], 'Robert': ['Q of hearts', '10 of hearts'], 'Steve': ['4 of spades', '5 of spades']?

function.name: poker_game_winner
function.description: Identify the winner in a poker game based on the cards. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

players.description: Names of the players in a list.

cards.description: An object containing the player name as key and the cards as values in a list.

type.description: Type of poker game. Defaults to 'Texas Holdem'

message.content: Alex is the winner. With only the two hole cards available, Alex’s “A♠ K♠” gives him the highest card (an Ace) and beats the other hands.
message.reasoning:
We need to determine winner in Texas Hold'em with only two hole cards each, no community cards provided. In Texas Hold'em, you need 5-card hand from 7 cards (2 hole + 5 community). But community cards not given. So maybe they assume no community cards? Or maybe they assume the two cards are the only cards? But that would be like a 2-card hand, which is not standard. The question likely expects to evaluate best 5-card hand from the two cards only? That doesn't make sense.

Maybe they want to compare the two-card hands as if they were the only cards? In that case, highest card wins. Alex has A♠ K♠, highest A. Robert Q♥ 10♥, highest Q. Steve 5♠ 4♠, highest 5. Sam 3♣ 2♦, highest 3. So Alex wins. But maybe they consider straight or flush? Alex has A♠ K♠, not a flush because only two spades. But if we consider only two cards, no flush. So Alex wins.

Thus answer: Alex.
